newsitem.title: MONACO: MOTOR RACING-AMBITIOUS LIGIER UNVEIL NEW CAR.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-AMBITIOUS LIGIER UNVEIL NEW CAR.

text.p: After covering a few laps of the casino square in Monte Carlo in the new Ligier JS 45 on Tuesday, Olivier Panis said he hoped to drive the car the victory at least once in this year's Formula One world championship.
"To win one race or more and to finish regularly in the points will be our goal this season," said Frenchman Panis, who handed Ligier their sole victory last year by winning the Monaco Grand Prix.
"It was just fantastic to win here," he said. "I think the car will be even more competitive this season."

Panis and new team mate Shinji Nakano of Japan, who replaces Brazilian Pedro Diniz, now with Damon Hill in the TWR Arrows team, had earlier removed the cover from the navy blue JS 45, apparently similar to last year's car.

"Improvements have been made in some sections," said Ligier managing director Bruno Michel. "We were not happy with the brakes and that's one thing that has been worked on but the engine is also more powerful."
Ligier will use this year a new configuration of the Mugen Honda V10 engine and further changes will be brought to the car before the season starts.
"Externally, the back of the car will be slightly different from what you see," said Michel, hinting a new aileron might be fitted.

The French team, who have won nine races since their F1 debut in 1976, were bought by Benetton boss Flavio Briatore in 1994 and finished sixth in last year's constructors' championship with 15 points.
"A lot of progress has been made and I believe we can go even further," said Italian Briatore.
He confirmed he was having talks with Frenchman Alain Prost, seeking to take over Ligier in his bid to put together an all-French team.
"We are talking and I hope we will reach an agreement but I don't know when," he said.

The negotiations between Briatore and Prost, hoping to power the Ligier car with a Peugeot engine, have been slowed down by doubts over the future of this year's French Grand Prix, clouded by a row over television rights, a reliable source close to Ligier said.
Briatore, looking forward to an agreement which would allow him to concentrate on the Benetton team, said Ligier would continue anyway.
"If there is an agreement, very well, but if not, we will continue to work," he said. "Ligier is now almost a top team and can still improve."
